title: Ensuring Better Oversight of Public Expenditures
what_it_is: Ensuring Better Oversight of Public Expenditures

sections.label: SPH Media and Sports Hub funding
sections.summary: The passage states $900 million funds SPH Media Trust over five years and $1.5 billion terminates the Sports Hub partnership, totalling $2.4 billion of taxpayers' money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first one is the $900 million for funding the SPH Media Trust over the next five years and the second is the $1.5 billion to terminate the public-private partnership operating the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is a total of $2.4 billion of taxpayers' money.

sections.label: Assets sold and cash left
sections.summary: The passage states assets were sold for $3.9 billion after restructuring, with only $110 million of cash and shares left to fund the loss-making media business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These assets were sold for $3.9 billion after the restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But only $110 million of cash and shares were left behind to fund the loss-making media business and taxpayers will be footing the rest of the bill moving forward.

sections.label: Sports Hub termination cost breakdown
sections.summary: The passage states the $1.5 billion termination cost to SHPL comprises $300 million for open market value and $1.2 billion for outstanding loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second significant expense incurred by taxpayers is the $1.5 billion contract termination cost to be paid to Sports Hub Pte Ltd (SHPL), which is said to comprise $300 million for the open market value of the Sports Hub and $1.2 billion for taking over the outstanding loans taken up by SHPL for the construction of the Sports Hub.

sections.label: Estimated annual financing payments
sections.summary: The passage states that at 4%, estimated annual financing payments should be about $90 million a year from 2014 to 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At 4%, I estimated that the annual financing payments should only be about $90 million a year from 2014 to 2035.

sections.label: Estimated outstanding liabilities to SHPL
sections.summary: The passage estimates an outstanding loan of $920 million and reserves of $320 million, so the Government should pay $600 million, not $1.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To sum up, I have estimated an outstanding loan of $920 million and total accumulated reserves of $320 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government should only be paying the difference between the two amounts, which is $600 million, as outstanding financial liabilities to SHPL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This $600 million figure is definitely much lower than the $1.2 billion agreed by the Government to pay SHPL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to seek clarifications from the Minister to justify the $1.5 billion termination cost to be paid to SHPL.

sections.label: Ministerial statement on Sports Hub
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Edwin Tong explained MCCY terminated the PPP agreement so the Government could take over ownership and management of the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the Sports Hub, Minister Edwin Tong explained in his Ministerial Statement on 1 August 2022 that MCCY decided to terminate the public-private partnership (PPP) agreement as the interests of Singapore and Singaporeans would be better served by the Government taking over the ownership and management of the Sports Hub.

sections.label: Termination sum basis explained
sections.summary: Mr Leong Mun Wai claims the $1.5 billion termination sum is too high, but Minister Edwin Tong already explained its basis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai claims that the termination sum of $1.5 billion is too high but Minister Edwin Tong had already explained the basis for this figure.

sections.label: Transaction financially neutral
sections.summary: The transaction is financially neutral because SHPL is not paid more than what would otherwise have been committed under the PPP model.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In other words, the entire transaction is financially neutrally because we are not paying SHPL more than what we would otherwise have committed to under the PPP model.

sections.label: SPH shareholders injection for SMT
sections.summary: Mr Leong Mun Wai asked why SPH shareholders cannot pay more, but Minister Josephine Teo explained shareholders voted for an $80 million cash and $30 million share injection for SMT.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai asked why SPH shareholders cannot pay more.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But Minister Josephine Teo has already explained that the shareholders voted and agreed to an injection of $80 million in cash and $30 million worth of shares for SMT.

sections.label: PAP financial probity watchwords
sections.summary: Since first elected 60 years ago, the PAP Government has made financial probity, honesty, prudence, incorruptibility and transparency its watchwords.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since the People's Action Party (PAP) Government was first elected 60 years ago, we have made financial probity, honesty, prudence, incorruptibility and transparency our watchwords.

sections.label: Prudent public funds without borrowing
sections.summary: This was done without borrowing, through consistent care and prudence with public funds, despite Opposition calls to save less and spend more.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Unlike other governments, we did this without having to borrow.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This was not serendipitous and it was not by chance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We were able to do so only because we have been consistently careful and prudent with public funds and this is so, despite repeated calls by the Opposition, Mr Leong Mun Wai included, to save less and spend more, use more of the reserves, draw more than 50% of the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For our part, the PAP Government will continue to exercise prudence in our public expenditure and act, as always, in the interest of Singaporeans and Singapore.

sections.label: Government support for SPH Media Trust
sections.summary: The answer is no; Government support for SPH Media Trust is to have media with a Singaporean lens and to preserve vernacular media.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With respect to the first question, or clarification, the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What Mr Leong fails to understand is that the support put in by the Government for SPH Media Trust is because there are certain things that we hold dear.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: One, it is to have a media that can see things through a Singaporean lens and that can report things from a domestic viewpoint.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The second thing is to preserve our vernacular media.
